To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
In patients with primary aldosteronismo, the parathyroid gland is activated, and the parathyroid hormone (PTH) level is elevated.

1) primary aldosteronismo (PA) is characterized by an abnormal calcium metabolism, with a higher level of parathyroid hormone (PTH) and a lower level of ionized calcium, 2) the abnormal calcium metabolism of PA is associated with a lower level of serum magnesium and a higher level of serum phosphate, 3) the alterations of calcium metabolism in PA patients are reversed by spironolac-tone and by surgical removal of the aldosterone-producing adenoma,

patients with primary aldosteronisms (PA) have a higher serum parathyroid hormone (sPTH) level than normotensive healthy individuals, and that both sPTH level and blood pressure decrease after the treatment of PA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of calcium metabolism in primary aldoster-onism, and its reversal by spirono-lactone or by the surgical removal of adrenocortical adenomas.
the effects of aldosterone on parathyroid hormone (PT) and calcium homeostasis.

the study of the effects of spiro-nolactone administration and the surgical removal (adrenalectomy) of aldosterone-producing adrenal adenomas on the plasma levels of calcium and PTH in primary aldoster-onism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the alterations of calcium metabolism and parathyrin function in PA are due to a direct effect of the increased aldosterone levels on the renal handling of calcium, and to an increase in the serum ionized calcium level, which in turn induces a secondary increase of the serum intact parathyrin concentration.

the calcium/PTH alterations observed in the PA patients were due to a combination of factors, including the presence of hyperaldosteronism, the presence of hypertension, and the possible presence of a primary parathyroid dysfunction.
the alterations of calcium and parathyroid hormone metabolism are more evident in PA than in EH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PA is associated with a mild form of secondary hyperparathyroidism, and that the treatment of the PA patients with spironolactones or with the surgical removal of the adenoma is followed by a decrease in the PTH level and by a normalization of the serum ionized calcium level.
in patients with PA there is a state of mild hyperparathyroidism, which is reversed after the administration of spironolac-tone or by surgical treatment.

the alterations in Ca metabolism and parathyroids function observed in PA are probably due to the chronic stimulation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and that the correction of these abnormalities is obtained by the removal of the stimulus (surgical removal of the adenoma) and by spironolctone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PA patients have higher serum PTH than normotensive and hypertensive subjects.
the surgical removal of adrenal adenomas or treatment with spironolactones can improve calcium metabolism in patients with PA.

in PA patients, the increase in serum ionised calcium and the decrease in PTH levels are associated both with the administration of spironolac tone and with the surgical removal of an aldosterone-producing adenoma, thus suggesting that the alterations of calcium metabolism and parathyrin function observed in these patients are due to the presence of aldosterone excess.
